title: Stainless steel cleaning paste
subtitle: A gentle abrasive paste for sinks, hobs, and pans
excerpt: A thick paste of bicarbonate of soda and castile soap for removing water spots, grease, and light staining from stainless steel surfaces. Applied with a damp cloth, rubbed with the steel's grain, then rinsed. Makes about 200 g of paste. Shelf life 3 months.
sourceNotes: Bicarb (sodium bicarbonate) as a mild abrasive: Mohs hardness ~2.5, which is below stainless steel (Mohs 5.5-6.3). Scratches steel if used cross-grain; always rub with the grain to avoid visible scratch patterns. Castile soap as the liquid binder: saponified plant oils, emulsifies grease. Cream of tartar (potassium bitartrate) added optionally at 2-3% to boost acidic cleaning action on rust spots. Dish soap is an alternative binder to castile soap for a degreasing variant. Lemon EO (optional): limonene content provides mild degreasing and scent.

recipe.batchNotes: 200 g is roughly a 3-month supply for a single sink. Scale to fill a 400 ml jar.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready immediately. Stir or shake before each use as the paste settles.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 3 months sealed in a jar. Bicarb is stable; the castile soap can go rancid if exposed to air and light. Stir before use.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cleaning ingredient with a particle hardness lower than the surface being cleaned, so it lifts deposits through friction without scratching. Bicarbonate of soda (Mohs hardness ~2.5) is mild enough for stainless steel (Mohs ~5.5-6.3) when used with the grain.

content.text: Combine all ingredients in a bowl and stir to a thick paste. Transfer to a wide-mouth jar.
To use: scoop a small amount onto a damp cloth or sponge. Rub onto the stainless steel surface with the grain, follow the direction of the brushed finish, not across it.
Rinse thoroughly with warm water. Dry with a clean cloth to prevent water spots.
3 months in a sealed jar. The paste settles on standing, stir before use. Discard if it develops an off or rancid smell from the soap.
